title: Rain-free Chilean streams rose after strong earthquake shaking: at seismic energy density of 1 J/m3 or more, 43% of gauges rose by 20% or more against 9% in placebo windows (CAMELS-CL, 1979-2016)
abstract: Question: Do streams rise after earthquake shaking more often than chance when rain is measured, and at which seismic energy density e? A campaign study of US gauges (sci:sha256:960bb4a1...) found an excess at e of 1 J/m3 or more, but it had no rain data. Approach: We used CAMELS-CL daily streamflow and CR2MET catchment rain for 516 Chilean catchments and 453 declustered ComCat mainshocks (M 5 or more, depth 70 km or less, 1979-2016). We used the US response rule (a rise of 20% or more over the extrapolated recession on days 1 to 5) and added a rain rule (below 1 mm each day from day -7 to +5). The placebo was the same gauge in the same season of up to 30 other years. We wrote the plan before we calculated outcomes. Findings: There were 2,250 rain-free eligible pairs. At e of 1 J/m3 or more, 42.9% of 163 pairs rose, against 9.3% of placebo windows (excess +33.7 points, 95% event-bootstrap interval +13.6 to +41.8, 16 events; real share above all 30 placebo years). Without the 2010 Maule earthquake the excess was +28.8 points (+6.6 to +44.5), and Valparaiso 1985 alone gave 9 of 13 rises against 4.5%. Below 0.1 J/m3 the excess was small and not clear; at 0.1 to 1 J/m3 it was +15.9 points (-0.8 to +31.3). Falls did not increase. With ShakeMap PGV the excess was +17 points at 3 to 10 cm/s and +38 at 10 to 30 cm/s. In windows that stayed rain-free to day 30, flow was about 26% above the placebo at days 10 to 20. After that the interval included zero, so we could not measure a recovery time. In an exploratory analysis, the most arid third of the catchments responded less (+19 against +47 to +50 points), and Tocopilla 2007 in the hyper-arid north gave no rises. Limitations: 16 strong events, of which Maule supplies 58% of pairs; epicentral e and model-based ShakeMap Atlas PGV ignore rupture geometry; gridded rain can miss local showers; many catchments are regulated; exploratory moderator tests are not corrected for multiplicity.
